findings.explanation: The resource omits service_account, so the version runs as PROJECT_ID@appspot.gserviceaccount.com (the App Engine default service account). In projects created before ~2019 this SA has the Editor primitive role at project level. HLD_GCP_189 only checks for the Compute Engine default SA, not the App Engine default SA, so this passes the engine. A dedicated least-privilege SA should be created and assigned just as HLD_PROPOSED_001 requires for Cloud Run.
findings.remediation: Add service_account = var.service_account to the resource and expose a service_account variable. In the example, create a google_service_account resource and pass its email.
findings.title: App Engine standard version has no service_account — defaults to the App Engine default SA which carries project Editor in older projects

findings.explanation: The handlers block sets url_regex and script_path but omits the login attribute, which defaults to LOGIN_OPTIONAL (no auth required). There is no google_app_engine_application resource in the module for HLD_GCP_190 (IAP must be enabled) to evaluate, so the check never fires. Any request reaching the App Engine URL is served without authentication — if the function is internal-only, callers from the public internet can invoke it.
findings.remediation: For internal-only use, add login = "LOGIN_REQUIRED" or login = "LOGIN_ADMIN" to the handlers block. For external access with auth, create a google_app_engine_application resource with iap { enabled = true } and expose it through the module.
findings.title: URL handler has no login requirement and no IAP — application is publicly accessible without authentication

findings.explanation: The example sets rotation_period = "100000s" which is approximately 27.8 hours. All other KMS keys in related modules (cloudrun, cloudfunction2) use 7776000s (90 days). An excessively short rotation period in a real deployment would trigger continuous re-encryption of all bucket objects and could exhaust KMS quota or cause unexpected failures. This appears to be an accidental value rather than intentional testdata configuration.
findings.remediation: Change rotation_period to "7776000s" (90 days) to match the standard used across other modules in this repository.
findings.title: KMS key rotation_period = 100000s (≈28 hours) in example — far below the standard 90-day minimum, will cause excessive re-encryption

suggested_policies.rationale: google_app_engine_standard_app_version has only one existing policy (HLD_GCP_189, Compute Engine default SA). The App Engine default SA (PROJECT_ID@appspot.gserviceaccount.com) is not the Compute Engine default SA and is not covered. In older GCP projects it holds the Editor primitive role. The same explicit-SA pattern has been codified for Cloud Run (HLD_PROPOSED_001), Cloud Run v2 jobs (HLD_GCP_264), Cloud Functions (HLD_GCP_179), Cloud Scheduler (HLD_GCP_266), and Cloud Workflows (HLD_GCP_267). Adding it for App Engine standard completes the coverage.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_004
name: App Engine standard versions must have an explicit service account configured
principle: identity-and-access
severity: HIGH
rationale: |
  When service_account is omitted, the version runs as the App Engine default
  service account (PROJECT_ID@appspot.gserviceaccount.com). In projects created
  before 2019 this SA holds the Editor primitive role at project level, giving
  the running application broad read/write access to all project resources.
  A dedicated least-privilege service account should always be assigned
  explicitly, consistent with the same requirement for Cloud Run, Cloud
  Functions, and Cloud Workflows.
remediation: |
  Add an explicit service_account to the resource:
  ```hcl
  resource "google_app_engine_standard_app_version" "app" {
    service_account = google_service_account.app.email
    ...
  }
  ```
resources:
  google_app_engine_standard_app_version:
    path: service_account
    not_null: true
